Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates asymmetry in pulmonary vascularity with a smaller, oligemic right lung and prominent left hilar structures, which are chronic radiographic signs of longstanding right pulmonary artery obstruction or stenosis. This finding is consistent with the vascular involvement seen in Takayasu arteritis and is confirmed by the calcified stenosis/occlusion of the right pulmonary artery shown on the CT scan (Figure 2b).
